records.failureSummary: Delivered the runtime configuration and stdout logging foundation modules (backend only: src/config.js, src/logger.js). config.js resolves PORT (default 3000) and DATA_DIR (default ./data; container injects /data) from the environment via a pure loadConfig(env) function, plus a memoized getConfig() and an import-time config snapshot. Environment values are treated as untrusted: PORT is trimmed and validated as an integer in 0..65535 and fails fast with a descriptive ConfigError (code INVALID_CONFIG) when malformed, DATA_DIR is trimmed, defaults on blank input and rejects NUL bytes, and an absolute dataDirPath is derived from the normalized value. The normalized object is frozen and also exposes PORT/DATA_DIR aliases plus named port/dataDir/dataDirPath exports. logger.js emits newline-delimited structured JSON to stdout (debug/info) and stderr (warn/error) only, with injectable streams for verification; it never writes to a file and does not import any fs write API. Every payload is passed through a deep redactor before serialization: field names are matched by word (password, passwd, secret, token, apikey, key, authorization, cookie, session, credential, privatekey, signature, salt, hash, digest, otp, pin, jwt, including camelCase/snake/kebab variants), and free-form strings are scrubbed for Bearer tokens and inline password= [REDACTED] fragments. Errors, arrays, nested objects and circular references are handled. No passwords, tokens or secrets are ever emitted. Dependencies remain empty (Node standard library only); no API contract was changed and existing project scripts are untouched.
